what is the best browser to use if privacy is your concern and why? (2015)

It's not really just a browser but Tails. It's an OS that runs from a USB drive, which uses TOR and Firefox. It strips as many unique machine and software 'fingerprints' as possible. It's also open source, if I recall correctly, so it's easier to spot malicious compromises in the code.

Is TOR really still the go-to for privacy in terms of browsers? It's built on the firefox platform that is just abound with security issues, and haven't the NSA/CIA/etc infiltrated most of the TOR network and can still get your information? Or does Tails cover those flaws?

Tor is just basically a proxy and yes it can be broken, whether it is or not is debate-able. This helps conceal your IP address. Firefox will always have flaws (as will any software truthfully) all you can do is minimize the risk; which is what Tails is designed to accomplish, by having a temporary OS that disappears when you shut it down. They all look identical from the outside (assuming you don't alter it, which is recommended,) which allows you to maintain anonymity. It's essentially aims at eliminating any 'proof.' Pull the USB stick out and your back to your original set-up, and the USB OS isn't persistent so it wont contain trace evidence.
While nothing is perfect I believe what @catechumen said is correct. It is the best option at the moment if setup correctly and used properly.
